device.name: Philips Hue Bridge
device.notes: Hue Bridge v2 exposes a local HTTP REST API on port 80. GET /api/config returns bridge metadata without authentication. Control endpoints require a whitelist username created by POST /api while the physical link button is pressed. Discovery should prefer the Hue-specific mDNS service and fall back to UPnP/SSDP device description XML.

issued_to_client: API username (bearer-equivalent; sent in the URL path on plain HTTP)
credentials.notes: The username is transmitted in the URL on unencrypted HTTP and never expires on its own. Treat it as a long-lived LAN secret and delete unused whitelist entries.
stored_on_device: Whitelist usernames issued to paired clients
ZigBee network key for paired lights

factory_reset.effect: Clears every whitelist username and the bridge's own ZigBee network configuration. Paired bulbs stay joined to the old, now-forgotten network and must be re-added (or reset themselves) afterwards, so a bridge reset is a much bigger event than a WiFi device reset.

procedures.indicator: LEDs cycle and the bridge reboots.
procedures.name: Recessed restore button

steps.action: Press the recessed button on the underside of the bridge with a paperclip and hold until the LEDs cycle.
Wait for the bridge to reboot and re-acquire a DHCP lease.

methods.description: Plug the bridge into the router with Ethernet and power it. It takes a DHCP lease and starts answering mDNS/SSDP; there is no WiFi passphrase to transfer, so there is no setup AP and no credential encryption problem.

steps.action: Connect the bridge to the LAN over Ethernet and apply power.
steps.expect: All three front LEDs light; the bridge answers _hue._tcp.local.

methods.description: The bridge issues an API username (whitelist entry) to any client that asks within roughly 30 seconds of the physical link button being pressed. This is a proximity proof, not an account: no cloud login is involved and the username keeps working after the vendor cloud goes away.

steps.action: POST /api with a devicetype string to confirm the bridge rejects unauthorized clients.
steps.expect: Error type 101, 'link button not pressed' — proves the bridge is reachable and unpaired.

steps.action: Press the round link button on the top of the bridge.
Repeat POST /api within the pairing window.
steps.expect: success.username — store it; it is the only credential needed for all later control.

setup.notes: Two separate things have to happen before a client can control a Hue Bridge: the bridge has to reach the LAN (Ethernet only — the v2 bridge has no WiFi radio and no credential provisioning of its own), and the client has to be authorized by the physical link button. Only the second step is a protocol flow.

rejoin.notes: Moving the bridge to a different router is a cable move plus a new DHCP lease. Stored usernames survive, so previously authorized clients keep working; only the IP changes, which is why clients must key off the TXT bridgeid rather than the address.

http_endpoints.description: Unauthenticated bridge info including name, bridgeid, MAC, modelid, software version, API version, and network settings.
http_endpoints.name: Bridge Config

http_endpoints.description: Press-link pairing endpoint that creates a whitelist username when the bridge link button has been pressed.
http_endpoints.name: Create User

fields.description: Application identifier used for the created Hue whitelist username.
fields.name: devicetype
